cards.title: Spread beats with round brackets
cards.body: Write **bd(3,8)** and Strudel plays 3 kicks spread over 8 steps of the cycle. The first number sets how many beats play, the second how many steps they are spread over.

cards.title: Which pattern plays five kicks in every cycle?
cards.explanation: The first number counts the beats, so bd(5,8) plays five kicks in each cycle, spread over 8 steps. bd(3,5) plays three kicks over 5 steps.

cards.title: What plays in cycles 1 and 2?
options: c3 then e3, with no g3
c3, e3 and g3 in a row
g3 alone, then c3 with e3
c3 with g3, then e3 with g3
cards.explanation: The comma plays both sides at the same time. g3 sounds in every cycle, and <c3 e3> adds c3 in cycle 1 and e3 in cycle 2.

cards.title: Play c3, e3 and g3 together as one chord
cards.starterCode:
stack(
  s("bd ~ sd ~"),
  note("c3 e3 g3")
)
cards.passMsg: The three notes now start together as a chord.
cards.failMsg: Put a **comma** between the notes instead of a space.

cards.answer: It plays **one step per cycle**, moving to the next step each time round.

cards.title: Build a loop with a Euclid kick and a chord
cards.starterCode:
stack(
  s("bd*4, hh*8"),
  note("c2 ~ c2 g2")
)

rubric.label: Kick on a Euclid rhythm, like bd(3,8)
A chord: notes joined by commas

cards.title: Change speed with .fast and .slow
cards.body: **.fast(2)** squeezes a pattern so it plays twice in each cycle, and **.slow(2)** stretches it over two cycles. They do what * and / do inside mini-notation.
cards.snippetComment: // cycle 1 → c3 e3 · 2 → g3 b3 · 3 → c3 e3

cards.title: Which pattern plays the same as s("bd sd").fast(2)?
cards.explanation: [bd sd]*2 plays the pair twice in one cycle, as .fast(2) does. [bd sd]/2 is the slow version: bd in one cycle, sd in the next.

cards.title: What plays in cycles 1 and 2?
options: c3 e3 g3, then g3 e3 c3
g3 e3 c3, then c3 e3 g3
cards.explanation: .every(2, rev) applies rev to the first cycle and to every second cycle after it. So cycle 1 plays g3 e3 c3, reversed, and cycle 2 plays c3 e3 g3 as written.

cards.title: Reverse the second line every other cycle
cards.starterCode:
stack(
  s("bd ~ sd ~"),
  s("hh*2 cp hh")
)
cards.passMsg: The second line now plays backwards in every other cycle.
cards.failMsg: Chain **.every** onto the second line, with 2 and rev inside.

cards.prompt: What does a comma do in mini-notation?
cards.answer: It plays steps **at the same time**, so c3,e3,g3 is a chord.

cards.title: Layer two patterns with three transforms
cards.starterCode:
stack(
  s("bd ~ sd ~, hh*4"),
  note("c3 e3 g3 b3").slow(2).rev()
)

cards.title: Layer a changed copy with .off and .jux
cards.body: **.off** layers a copy of the pattern, shifted later in time and changed by the function you give it: here 1/8 of a cycle later and 12 higher, so c3 is followed by c4. **.jux** also layers a changed copy, with the original on the left and the copy on the right.
cards.snippetComment: // cycle 1 → c3 c4 · 2 → e3 e4 · 3 → g3 g4

cards.title: Which pattern plays the original on the left and a reversed copy on the right?
cards.explanation: jux(rev) keeps the pattern as written in the left channel and plays it reversed in the right channel. .rev() on its own reverses it with no left and right split.

cards.title: Which cutoff does the low-pass filter use?
cards.explanation: Each effect is used once per sound, so a later .lpf overrides the earlier value. Both bd and sd play with a cutoff of 2000.

cards.title: Give the snare line reverb with .room
cards.starterCode:
stack(
  s("bd ~ bd ~").lpf(800),
  s("~ sd ~ sd"),
  s("hh*8").gain(0.5)
)
cards.passMsg: Reverb is on. The number in .room sets its level, from 0 to 1.
cards.failMsg: Chain **.room** onto the snare line, with a level between 0 and 1.

cards.answer: **Three kicks**, spread over 8 steps of each cycle.

cards.title: Layer drums and a melody with effects
cards.starterCode:
stack(
  s("bd ~ sd ~, hh*8").jux(rev),
  note("c3 e3 g3 e3").lpf(1200)
)
